investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Production Kubernetes Cluster
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was left unschedulable: the two nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining four nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never reached a running state within the eval timeout window.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote-agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. Two nodes expose the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource but have no remaining allocatable capacity; four nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector. Preemption was also exhausted (no preemption victims found). Because the pod never scheduled, the agent VM was never provisioned, and the eval runner received no evidence to satisfy the expected-output contract (vmIdPresent=true, remoteState in [running, idle, ready]). This is an eval-observed infrastructure scheduling constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage — no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: [Most likely] kata.peerpods.io/vm extended-resource capacity on the two eligible nodes is fully consumed by existing remote-agent pods or other workloads, leaving zero allocatable slots for new pods.

[Likely] The two kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes are at their configured peer-pod limit (e.g., a node-level max-vm quota set in the kata-containers or peer-pods operator configuration), and no pods have terminated to free capacity.

[Possible] The four non-kata nodes have a node affinity or node selector mismatch (e.g., a label such as kata-runtime=true or peerpods=enabled is absent), reducing the schedulable pool to only 2 nodes and amplifying the capacity shortage.

[Possible] A recent scale-down or node failure reduced the number of kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes from a previously larger pool, leaving the cluster under-provisioned for the current remote-agent workload.
[Less likely] The pod's resource request for kata.peerpods.io/vm was recently increased (e.g., requesting more than 1 VM unit per pod), causing previously sufficient nodes to appear insufficient.

recommendedNextActions: Immediately check kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity on the two eligible nodes (kubectl describe nodes) to confirm the pool is exhausted and determine the current headroom.
Identify and clean up any stale, stuck, or leaked remote-agent pods that may be holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots without serving active workloads.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe nodes showed kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity available (allocatable > 0 and requests < allocatable) on the two eligible nodes, the root cause would not be capacity exhaustion and a different scheduling constraint would need to be identified.

If a subsequent eval run of remote-agent-create succeeded and returned vmIdPresent=true with remoteState in [running, idle, ready], the scheduling issue would be transient rather than a sustained capacity shortage.

If the pod's node affinity selector were found to be misconfigured (e.g., referencing a label that no node carries at all), the root cause would shift from capacity exhaustion to a configuration error in the pod spec.

If only remote-agent-create failed while remote-agent-state and remote-agent-runtime passed, a shared scheduling constraint would be less likely and the failure would be localized to the create path specifically.

If the cluster had more than 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes and the message was produced by a transient node condition (e.g., node NotReady), the root cause would be node availability rather than sustained capacity exhaustion.
followUpEvals: Add a dedicated eval check that probes kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. requested capacity across all cluster nodes and fails when utilization exceeds a configurable threshold (e.g., 80%), providing early warning before full exhaustion.
Add a node-affinity coverage eval that verifies at least N nodes match the remote-agent pod's node selector/affinity, alerting when the eligible node count drops below a minimum threshold.
Add a stale-pod detection eval that identifies remote-agent pods stuck in Pending or Running state beyond a TTL, which would catch leaked VM slot holders before they exhaust capacity.

Extend the remote-agent-create check to capture and surface the Kubernetes scheduler event message as structured evidence (e.g., schedulerMessage, eligibleNodeCount, insufficientResourceNodes) so future failures are self-describing without requiring a separate kubectl probe.

investigation.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing Due to Kubernetes kata.peerpods.io/vm Resource Exhaustion
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api with identical Kubernetes scheduler messages indicating that the cluster's kata.peerpods.io/vm resource is exhausted on the 2 eligible nodes, and the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because no agent pod could be scheduled, the eval runner's createAgent call never returned a live agent, so no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was ever written and the expected-output contract was fully unmet.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity: only 2 nodes carry this resource and both are fully consumed, while the other 4 nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector. Every remote-agent pod submitted during the eval window was left Unschedulable for ~135–151 seconds before the probes timed out. Because pod scheduling never succeeded, the eval runner could not create a remote agent, and therefore could not poll agent state, leaving all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) absent. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity failure localized to the remote-agents Kubernetes scheduling layer; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Production Kubernetes Cluster
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was left unschedulable: the two nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining four nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never reached a running state within the eval timeout window.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote-agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. Two nodes expose the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource but have no remaining allocatable capacity; four nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector. Preemption was also exhausted (no preemption victims found). Because the pod never scheduled, the agent VM was never provisioned, and the eval runner received no evidence to satisfy the expected-output contract (vmIdPresent=true, remoteState in [running, idle, ready]). This is an eval-observed infrastructure scheduling constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage — no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: [Most likely] kata.peerpods.io/vm extended-resource capacity on the two eligible nodes is fully consumed by existing remote-agent pods or other workloads, leaving zero allocatable slots for new pods.

[Likely] The two kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes are at their configured peer-pod limit (e.g., a node-level max-vm quota set in the kata-containers or peer-pods operator configuration), and no pods have terminated to free capacity.

[Possible] The four non-kata nodes have a node affinity or node selector mismatch (e.g., a label such as kata-runtime=true or peerpods=enabled is absent), reducing the schedulable pool to only 2 nodes and amplifying the capacity shortage.

[Possible] A recent scale-down or node failure reduced the number of kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes from a previously larger pool, leaving the cluster under-provisioned for the current remote-agent workload.
[Less likely] The pod's resource request for kata.peerpods.io/vm was recently increased (e.g., requesting more than 1 VM unit per pod), causing previously sufficient nodes to appear insufficient.
